title: The Diet of Paradise and Human Dominion
english: Regarding seed-eating food, God commands this in these things: for those entering into paradise do not eat grass, but every tree beautiful for sight and good for food, and above all, from the tree of life, Christ who gives life. And these animals are to say that these beasts are nations gathered together in the Church by God, or that [the place of] horse-breeding and ox-feeding and camel-standing and sheep-rearing [...] today paradise exists.

Not so, O philosopher, but rather to say to God: 'let them rule all the earth' (Gen 1:26), and: 'let them have dominion over it and over all those in it' (Gen 1:28); this is the Lord's [purpose] in making man according to the image of God and letting him rule all the earth.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG 18 In Genesim de creatione u01-rem-early

title: Man as Second Ruler
english: Since God rules all the earth and all things in it, just as He does, so also He established man as a second ruler of all the earth and all things in it; this I say is to become man according to the image of God and according to likeness.
And God said, 'Let us make man according to our image and according to likeness' (Genesis 1:26). But toward whom did He say, 'Let us seek, O philosopher?'
For in saying, 'And God said, Let us make man according to our image and according to likeness,' He introduced a question for us to perceive: toward whom was He saying, 'Let us make?'
For having said, 'And God said, Let us make man,' He followed by saying, 'And God made man, according to the image of God He made him' (Genesis 1:27).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG 18 In Genesim de creatione u01-rem-mid

title: The Co-Creator and Shared Divinity
english: He made them male and female (Genesis 1:27). Therefore, the significance of the 'let us make' signifies being a co-creator and introduces a co-attendant.

For just as God the Father is the one who said, 'let us make man' (Genesis 1:26), so God is also toward whom the 'let us make' was spoken, being of one divinity of both persons: both the one saying, 'let us make man in our image and likeness' (Genesis 1:26), and the one making the man.

For the voice of 'let us make' presents the most holy and unchangeable divinity of the Father and the Son, [as being] the same as the divinity of the one who makes; for the image of God is simple and indivisible, being fire by nature.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
